source.note: Defects found in the Java bin grid implementation (POST v3/convertBinGrid) that concern the computation; those of its JSON handling (D1, D6 to D12, D17) are outside this package and not listed. Each defect listed has at least one test marked @pytest.mark.java_defect(<id>) that states the correct behaviour and failed before the Python implementation existed. Paths are relative to the repository root.

defects.title: Bin widths ignore the scale factor that the formulas then apply
docs: EPSG Guidance Note 7-2, methods 9666 and 1049: bin width is a ground distance and k scales it to the map grid
defects.defect: Bin widths are derived as map-grid distances but both conversion directions multiply them by k, so any k other than 1 reports a spurious squaring error ((span/2)(1 - 1/k) bins) and moves the squared corners by a factor k about the centre.
defects.expected: bin width = increment * grid distance / (node span * k); deriving, applying and inverting round-trips exactly for any k.

defects.title: The inline/crossline layout of the corners is never validated
defects.defect: Corners are sorted and labelled without checking that they are (minI,minJ), (minI,maxJ), (maxI,minJ), (maxI,maxJ); duplicate or repeated inline numbers divide by zero and produce NaN or infinity instead of the documented validation error.
defects.expected: InvalidCornersError naming the offending inline/crossline pairs.

defects.title: Degenerate or twisted corner geometry is not detected
defects.defect: Coincident corners give zero-length edges and atan2(0, 0); corners whose coordinates contradict their labels (crossing edges) give a meaningless bearing and handedness; non-finite coordinates propagate.
defects.expected: DegenerateBinGridError for zero-length edges, non-convex or self-intersecting corner sets, and non-finite coordinates.

defects.title: A bin grid in a non-projected CRS is accepted
docs: local/crs-conversion-service/docs/v3/tutorial/CRS_Convert_Service_howto.md#L3807 (section 7.3: BinGrids should use type BoundProjected or Projected)
defects.defect: Nothing checks the CRS type, so geographic coordinates in degrees are treated as linear map-grid coordinates.
defects.expected: UnsupportedCRSError unless the CRS is projected (optionally bound) with easting/northing value axes.

defects.title: No SpatialArea outline is produced, and the documented ring is clockwise
defects.defect: Section 7.2 promises a polygon for the SeismicBinGrid SpatialArea, which the code never builds; the section 7.5 example ring A,B,D,C,A is clockwise for its coordinates although the section requires counterclockwise.
defects.expected: A closed, counterclockwise 5-point outline of the squared corners, in the map CRS and in WGS 84, returned as SpatialArea.

defects.title: The request is mutated and the input corners are lost
defects.defect: outBinGrid is the request's inBinGrid object, overwritten in place with converted and then squared coordinates.
defects.expected: The input is never modified; results keep the input, converted and squared corners side by side.

defects.title: A conversion is applied even when toCRS is the CRS the grid is in
defects.defect: Any non-empty toCRS sends the corners through a conversion.
defects.expected: No conversion, and no conversion recorded, when the target equals the source CRS.

defects.title: Rounding is inconsistent between corners and P6 origin
docs: SDU note 'Storage, compute and display precision'
defects.defect: Squared corner coordinates are rounded to 3 decimals while P6BinGridOriginEasting/Northing, which is corner A, is left unrounded, so the two disagree.
defects.expected: Full precision in the core; one output precision applied alike to corners and P6 origin; bin widths and bearing never rounded.

defects.title: The request's scale factor is written back, even into another CRS
docs: local/crs-conversion-service/docs/v3/tutorial/CRS_Convert_Service_howto.md#L3798 (section 7.2.3: ignored on input, populated with a derived value on output)
local/PROJ/docs/source/operations/transformations/affine.rst#L72-L73 (the point scale factor of the map grid)
defects.defect: P6ScaleFactorOfBinGrid is read from the request and written back unchanged; with toCRS it is the source projection's scale stamped on a grid in the target projection (UTM 15N's 0.9996 on BLM 14N, whose scale there is 1.0047), and with D2 any value other than 1 also moves the squared corners.
defects.expected: The request's value is ignored; the output scale factor is derived from the output CRS, so that the bin widths are the ground spacing of the bins in any CRS.
